title: Full triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category with shift $[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. A *full triangulated subcategory* of $\mathcal T$ is a full subcategory $\mathcal S$, given by a property $P$ of objects, such that the zero object is in $\mathcal S$ (up to isomorphism), $K\in\mathcal S$ implies $K[n]\in\mathcal S$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K,M\in\mathcal S$ the object $L$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathcal S$. Such an $\mathcal S$, with the shift and the distinguished triangles of $\mathcal T$ whose vertices lie in $\mathcal S$, is a pre-triangulated category, triangulated when $\mathcal T$ is, and the inclusion is an exact functor.
